How it is held varies by region: in northern Europe it is mostly held at the shoulder, in southern Europe and North Africa on the lap with the bow gripped from below. Begin by checking the number of strings and the tuning; most have three strings, often tuned in fifths. Because the bridge is fairly flat, several strings can be bowed at once. The sources differ on whether it has frets, so you have to judge by the individual instrument.

By region it can be confirmed as belonging to Middle Eastern, European and North African traditions, but the material details are still to be filled in.

雷貝克弓琴是中世紀與早期文藝復興的弓弦樂器，13至16世紀流行。其進入西歐與阿拉: The rebec is a bowed string instrument of the Middle Ages and the early Renaissance, popular from the 13th to the 16th century. Its entry into Western Europe coincided with the Arab conquest of the Iberian peninsula; in 9th-century eastern Europe bowed instruments already existed, and the Persian geographer Ibn Khurradadhbih mentions the Byzantine lyra as the equivalent of the Arab rebab. The name appears around the beginning of the 14th century, coming from Middle French and going back further to Arabic. It was used in Arab classical music, Moroccan Arabo-Andalusian music and Ottoman tea houses. The body is carved from a single block of wood; early forms mostly had two strings, three became common later, and larger versions were developed for 16th-century consorts. After the Renaissance it was gradually replaced by the viol, but it is still used in the folk music of eastern Europe, Spain, Portugal, Brazil and North Africa.
雷貝克弓琴的聆聽場合從中世紀宴會與專業吟遊樂手的演奏開始，亦見於阿拉伯古典音樂、: Listening to the rebec begins with medieval feasts and the playing of professional minstrels; it is also found in Arab classical music, Moroccan Arabo-Andalusian music, Ottoman tea houses and 16th-century rebec consorts. Later it was used for teaching dance, in the folk music of eastern Europe and Spain, in North African Andalusi nubah and the Chilote waltz of Chile, and it survives in the folk music of Portugal and Brazil. Modern recordings and performances include the early line-up of the Michael Nyman Band, medieval music groups, and 'Kingfisher' on Joanna Newsom's album Have One On Me; Alkan's Concerto for Solo Piano, Op. 39 Nos. 8-10, marks 'Quasi-ribeche' to imitate its sound.
雷貝克弓琴音色明亮尖銳，具有穿透力強的特點，帶有中世紀的古樸氣質。其音色介於小提: The rebec's timbre is bright and sharp, with strong carrying power, and it has the plain manner of the Middle Ages. Its sound lies between the violin and the flute: it keeps the warmth of a string instrument without losing the clarity of a wind. The narrow boat-shaped body decides how it resonates; the volume is relatively small but the texture is fine, and the range sits mainly in the upper middle register. Next to the modern violin the rebec sounds plainer and rougher, lacking the violin's roundness and rich overtones. Its sound carries a sense of history and of place, and in medieval music it often gives a mysterious, deep atmosphere; it suits classical and traditional styles.
